source.title: Platonic Representations for Poverty Mapping: Unified Vision-Language Codes or Agent-Induced Novelty?
source.authors: Satiyabooshan Murugaboopathy; C. Jerzak; Adel Daoud

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-modal representational alignment in a new poverty-mapping setting using CCA-aligned cosine similarities, a conceptual test rather than a reproduction of the original method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many wealth-prediction outcomes, but they are not rows here because they measure prediction performance rather than representational convergence. The reported similarity results are the matched NMR–CV cosine analysis and its regional analysis.
record.test_reason: The study measures partial representational alignment and geographic variation in a new poverty-mapping setting, bearing on V7 and V6. It does not measure alignment increasing with model capability.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors find moderate, partial vision–text alignment after CCA, broadly consistent with but insufficient to establish a single shared latent representation. They also conclude that evidence for agent-induced novelty is limited.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CCA followed by cosine similarity on paired DHS image/text embeddings in a poverty-mapping domain; does not reproduce a scale-dependent alignment test.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported alignment varies geographically, with localized clusters of higher similarity and stronger alignment among geographically proximate regions.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Social Computing (ICSC 2026), Communications in Computer and Information Science, Springer Nature (as stated in the citation)
record.problems: The alignment result is moderate and measured after CCA; the specific model variants used for the alignment analysis are not stated. The study does not relate alignment to model size or performance, compare alternative similarity measures, or test whether shared training data/objectives explain the alignment. The regional result is described qualitatively from a figure.
record.rows_left_out: Wealth-prediction performance results in Figure 3 and Tables A.I.1–A.I.2, and related spatial/temporal prediction comparisons, are excluded because they measure predictive performance rather than representational similarity. Figure A.I.3 is not separately recorded because the text does not describe its result beyond the caption.

untested.parts: Alignment increasing with model size or capability across independently trained models. The model-size analysis concerns wealth-prediction performance.
Increasing image-caption alignment as both vision and language models improve; no alignment comparison across capability levels is reported.
Shared features or subspaces across independently initialized networks of the same architecture.
Representation substitution or transfer with little loss. Fitting CCA alone does not test interchangeability.
Recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.

Dependence on alternative similarity metrics or their settings, and weakening or disappearance under controlled input changes or out-of-distribution evaluation. Prediction results on country and time holdouts do not measure representation alignment.
Alignment plateauing with scale, and shared training data or objectives explaining the alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The random-pairing comparison establishes above-null matched similarity, not convergence with capability. CCA is fitted on training data and similarity evaluated on held-out clusters, but the text's reference to a first component leaves the precise cosine calculation insufficiently specified. Figure A.I.3 is already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No scale sweep of representation alignment across model sizes or capability levels, nor comparison of independently trained models across architectures, objectives, or data.
Measures cross-modal similarity for paired DHS clusters, but does not test whether alignment rises as both models improve or compare alignment across model-performance levels.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations, features, or shared subspaces.
CCA alignment is used to measure similarity; the study does not test whether representations can be transferred or substituted with little loss.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Reports geographic variation in aligned similarity, but does not compare similarity metrics or settings such as neighbour counts, and does not test out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports moderate, partial alignment and cautions against inferring a single shared representation. It does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared training data/objectives explain it.

rows.subject: NMR and CV embeddings (specific model variants for this analysis not stated)
rows.operation_detail: CCA-align NMR and CV embeddings, then measure cosine similarity for matched clusters

conditions.value: held-out clusters; CCA fit on training split

rows.measure: Cosine similarity between aligned NMR and CV embeddings
rows.baseline: Random-pairing baseline, including shuffled location pairs within the same country and survey year when available; numerical similarity not stated
rows.value: Median approximately 0.60; Figure 6 distribution μ=0.581; matched-pair comparison with random pairings: t=312.96, p<1e−10
rows.uncertainty: σ=0.106 for the Figure 6 distribution; t=312.96, p<1e−10 for comparison against random pairings
rows.locator: Results, Figure 6 and Validation of Intra-Cluster Similarity Against Null Distribution
rows.note: Authors characterize the alignment as moderate and partial, and explicitly caution that it does not establish convergence to a single shared latent representation.
rows.check: The median aligned cosine similarity is approximately 0.60, explicitly interpreted as moderate and partial. This observes V7's incomplete-alignment component; 'partial' incorrectly treats incompleteness as a failure of that challenge claim. Remove V2 because no capability-dependent alignment comparison is reported, and the text consists of location-year descriptions rather than image captions. Specific embedding variants remain unspecified.

rows.subject: NMR and CV embeddings (specific model variants for this analysis not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Compute a CCA-aligned cosine-similarity matrix for matched NMR–CV embeddings and sort by latitude
rows.value: Figure only; text reports localized clusters of higher similarity and stronger alignment among geographically proximate regions
rows.note: The text describes geographic structure in the alignment but gives no regional numerical values.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports geographically structured similarity, supporting the input-dependence component of V6 qualitatively. Regional magnitudes and uncertainty are unavailable. Remove V2 because no capability trend is measured and V7 because localized high-similarity clusters do not establish incomplete overall alignment.
